IV. MITIGATING MEASURES
There are several provisions of the proposed legislation which would allow for mitigation in some situations. The Secretary would have the authority to grant permits for up to one year, to import endangered species contracted prior to publication of the notice and where undue economic hardship could be proved. The Secretary would also be allowed to authorize the taking, importing, etc., of listed species for specific purposes such as zoological, scientific, or educational. Such authority would have a mitigating effect on the listing of a species with regard to the economic and cultural uses presently being made of animals.
The proposed legislation also provides for consultation with the States and countries involved prior to addition of a species to the list. Cooperation with the States may include consultation before Federal acquisition of land or water in that State.
The Secretary's authority to adopt special regulations dealing with those species likely to become threatened with extinction (Group 2) would allow for discretionary treatment of species appearing on that list. The effect could thus be controlled by the Secretary in such a manner as to maximize protection of the animal and at the same time support continued use of the animals for commercial, sporting, or cultural purposes.
